steps.label: Nodal map
steps.detail: Assign side and nodal level using explicit anatomic boundaries and name the map used.
steps.look: Axial contrast-enhanced images from skull base to clavicles; level boundaries: hyoid (II/III), cricoid (III/IV), posterior border of sternocleidomastoid (II–IV/V), submandibular gland (Ib).
steps.normal: No enlarged or morphologically abnormal cervical lymph nodes.
findings: Suspicious nodes at right level [II] and [III].
Retropharyngeal node on the [left] (level VIIa of the radiotherapy map).
Parotid (level VIII) node on the [ ].
steps.tip: The surgical and radiotherapy node maps differ; name the map and describe the location in words as well.

steps.label: Index nodes
steps.detail: Describe number, distribution and the largest and most suspicious nodes with measurements.
steps.look: Measure short axis and long axis on axial images; give series and image numbers.
findings: Node 1: right level IIa, __ mm short axis × __ mm long axis (series __ image __).
Multiple bilateral level II–IV nodes, largest __ mm.

steps.label: Nodal morphology
steps.detail: Assess necrosis, cystic change, calcification, shape, hilum and conglomeration.
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI for necrosis; ultrasound for hilum and cortex.
findings: Central necrosis in the level [II] node.
Cystic node in an adult: metastasis (e.g., HPV-associated oropharyngeal or thyroid carcinoma) must be excluded.
Round node with loss of the fatty hilum.
Conglomerate nodal mass __ × __ × __ mm.
steps.tip: A cystic lateral neck mass in an adult is a metastasis until proven otherwise, not a branchial cyst.

steps.label: Extranodal extension and vessels
steps.detail: Describe irregular margins, infiltration of adjacent tissue and vascular involvement with confidence.
steps.look: Nodal margins, surrounding fat and muscle; carotid and internal jugular vein relationship.
steps.normal: No imaging signs of extranodal extension; vessels free.
findings: Irregular nodal margin with infiltration of the sternocleidomastoid: extranodal extension suspected.
Carotid encasement over more than 270°.
Internal jugular vein compression / thrombosis.

steps.label: Primary site and staging pathway
steps.detail: Review mucosal, thyroid and salivary sites and name the primary-specific staging system.
steps.look: Pharyngeal mucosa, tonsils, tongue base, larynx, thyroid and salivary glands.
steps.normal: No primary lesion identified in the mucosal, thyroid or salivary sites.
findings: Asymmetric tonsillar mass on the [right], compatible with the primary site.
Unknown primary: [ ].
Airway compromise at [ ].

steps.label: Space of origin
steps.detail: Localise the epicentre to a named space above or below the hyoid.
steps.look: Axial T1 without fat suppression to see preserved fat planes; identify the parapharyngeal fat as the key landmark.
findings: Lesion centred in the [parapharyngeal / masticator / parotid / carotid / retropharyngeal / perivertebral / visceral] space.
Lesion extends from the suprahyoid to the infrahyoid neck.
steps.tip: The direction in which the parapharyngeal fat is displaced tells you the space of origin.

steps.label: Tissue characteristics
steps.detail: Describe composition, T1 and T2 signal, diffusion and enhancement.
steps.look: T1, T2, fat-suppressed post-contrast images and DWI.
findings: T2-bright, well-defined lesion with heterogeneous enhancement (pleomorphic adenoma pattern).
Flow voids with intense enhancement (paraganglioma: salt-and-pepper pattern).
Restricted diffusion with homogeneous enhancement (lymphoma pattern).
Non-enhancing fluid (cyst).

steps.label: Displacement pattern
steps.detail: Assess how fat planes and the carotid and jugular vessels are displaced.
steps.look: Axial images at the level of maximal lesion size.
findings: Parapharyngeal fat displaced [anteromedially / posterolaterally].
Carotid artery displaced anteriorly (post-styloid / carotid space lesion).
Internal and external carotid arteries splayed (carotid body paraganglioma).
steps.tip: Splaying of the internal and external carotid arteries at the bifurcation indicates a carotid body tumour.

steps.label: Spread and critical structures
steps.detail: Assess airway, skull base, perineural pathways and visceral extension.
steps.look: Coronal images to the skull base; foramina and nerves; airway calibre.
steps.normal: No airway compromise; skull base and neural pathways intact.
findings: Extension to the skull base through the [foramen ovale].
Airway narrowed to __ mm.
Invasion of the [larynx / thyroid].

steps.label: Nodes and complications
steps.detail: Review regional nodes, collections and venous thrombosis.
steps.look: Nodal levels; rim-enhancing collections; jugular veins.
steps.normal: No suspicious nodes, collection or thrombosis.
findings: Suspicious nodes at level [ ].
Retropharyngeal abscess __ mm with rim enhancement.
Internal jugular vein thrombosis.

model.reporting_aim: Relate the mass to the midline, hyoid, sternocleidomastoid and carotid space before describing its content.

steps.label: Location
steps.detail: Localise the mass relative to the midline, hyoid and neck spaces, with the child's age.
steps.look: Ultrasound first: midline versus lateral; relation to the hyoid, sternocleidomastoid and thyroid.
findings: Midline cystic mass at the level of the hyoid.
Lateral cystic mass anterior to the sternocleidomastoid at the angle of the mandible.
Posterior triangle multiloculated mass.
steps.tip: Location is the strongest clue: midline suggests thyroglossal duct or dermoid cyst; anterior to sternocleidomastoid suggests a second branchial cleft cyst.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Describe cystic or solid components, septa, debris and calcification.
steps.look: Ultrasound with high-frequency probe; MRI for deep extension.
findings: Unilocular cyst with thin wall and internal debris.
Multiloculated cystic mass with fluid levels (lymphatic malformation).
Solid mass with calcification (pilomatrixoma / teratoma / neuroblastoma).

steps.label: Vascularity
steps.detail: Assess internal and peripheral flow or enhancement and vessel relationships.
steps.look: Colour Doppler; contrast MRI when performed.
findings: Avascular cyst.
Hypervascular solid mass (infantile haemangioma pattern).
Venous malformation with phleboliths and slow flow.

steps.label: Anatomic connections
steps.detail: Look for a tract, gland of origin or other structural connection, and airway effect.
steps.look: Relation to the hyoid, thyroid, salivary glands and sternocleidomastoid.
findings: Cyst embedded in the strap muscles with a tract to the hyoid (thyroglossal duct cyst).
Fusiform enlargement of the sternocleidomastoid in an infant (fibromatosis colli).
Ectopic thyroid tissue with an empty thyroid bed.
steps.tip: Confirm a normal thyroid in its bed before a midline mass is removed; it may be the only thyroid tissue.

steps.label: Nodes and infection
steps.detail: Assess nodal patterns and inflammatory complications such as abscess.
steps.look: Nodes: hilum, shape, necrosis; surrounding fat; collections.
steps.normal: Reactive-appearing nodes only; no collection.
findings: Suppurative lymphadenitis with abscess __ mm.
Necrotic nodes with minimal surrounding inflammation (atypical mycobacterial pattern).
Multiple enlarged nodes without hila (lymphoma to be considered).

steps.label: Primary site
steps.detail: Identify the lesion epicentre, subsite and dimensions.
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced MRI or CT; separate tumour from retained secretions on T2 and post-contrast images.
findings: Mass in the [ ] measuring __ × __ × __ mm.
Enhancing tumour separate from T2-bright retained secretions in the obstructed sinus.
steps.tip: On MRI, retained secretions are T2-bright and non-enhancing; tumour is intermediate and enhances.

steps.label: Growth pattern and local invasion
steps.detail: Inspect fat planes, muscle, bone and cartilage, and whether growth is expansile or destructive.
steps.look: Bone windows on CT; T1 marrow signal on MRI.
findings: Destructive bone erosion (aggressive growth pattern).
Smooth expansile remodelling (slow-growing lesion).
Invasion of the [pterygoid muscles / orbit / cartilage].
steps.tip: Bone destruction suggests malignancy; smooth remodelling suggests a slow benign process such as a mucocele.

steps.label: Perineural spread
steps.detail: Review neural pathways and skull-base foramina for spread.
steps.look: Pterygopalatine fossa, foramen rotundum and ovale, Meckel cave; fat-suppressed post-contrast MRI.
steps.normal: No perineural spread.
findings: Obliteration of fat in the pterygopalatine fossa with enhancement along V2.
Enlargement and enhancement of the [ ] nerve through the foramen [ ].
steps.tip: Loss of fat in the pterygopalatine fossa is an early sign of perineural spread.

steps.label: Vessels and airway
steps.detail: Assess vessel encasement and airway compromise.
steps.look: Carotid arteries and internal jugular veins; airway calibre.
steps.normal: No vascular encasement or airway compromise.
findings: Carotid encasement of more than 270°.
Airway narrowed to __ mm.

steps.label: Nodes and other sites
steps.detail: Map regional nodes by level and look for additional lesions.
steps.look: Nodal levels I–V and retropharyngeal nodes.
steps.normal: No suspicious nodes; no second lesion.
findings: Necrotic level [II] node __ mm.
Cystic node from HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma.
Second primary in the [ ].

steps.label: Globes and preseptal tissues
steps.detail: Assess globe contour and size, lens, vitreous, retina, choroid, intraocular material and preseptal swelling.
steps.look: Axial and coronal thin sections; soft-tissue and bone windows for foreign body.
steps.normal: Globes normal in contour; lenses in place; no intraocular abnormality; no preseptal swelling.
findings: Globe rupture: flattened posterior contour (flat tyre sign) with intraocular haemorrhage.
Intraocular metallic foreign body in the [ ] globe.
Retinal / choroidal detachment.
Calcified intraocular mass in a child (retinoblastoma to be considered).
steps.tip: Exclude a metallic intraocular foreign body with CT before MRI after trauma.

steps.label: Orbital compartments
steps.detail: Localise any lesion or collection to the extraconal, conal or intraconal compartment and measure it.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images; the extraocular muscle cone defines the compartments.
steps.normal: No orbital mass or collection; no proptosis.
findings: Subperiosteal abscess along the [medial] orbital wall, __ × __ × __ mm.
Intraconal well-circumscribed mass with progressive fill-in enhancement (venous malformation pattern).
Lacrimal gland enlargement.

steps.label: Muscles and optic nerves
steps.detail: Describe extraocular muscle and tendon involvement and optic nerve or sheath findings.
steps.look: Coronal images for muscle bellies; axial and coronal fat-suppressed images for the optic nerve.
steps.normal: Extraocular muscles and optic nerves normal.
findings: Enlargement of the [inferior and medial rectus] bellies sparing the tendons (thyroid eye disease pattern).
Muscle enlargement including the tendon with fat stranding (orbital inflammation).
Optic nerve sheath enhancement (tram-track sign, meningioma pattern).
Optic neuritis: enhancement and T2 signal of the [ ] optic nerve.
steps.tip: Thyroid eye disease enlarges the muscle bellies and spares the tendons; inflammation involves the tendon.

steps.label: Orbital apex and intracranial extension
steps.detail: Inspect the orbital apex, optic canal, superior orbital fissure, cavernous sinus and intracranial spread.
steps.look: Coronal and axial images at the apex; post-contrast MRI of the cavernous sinus.
steps.normal: Orbital apex, optic canal and cavernous sinus normal.
findings: Crowding of the orbital apex with optic nerve compression.
Cavernous sinus thrombosis (filling defect and expansion).
Intracranial extension through the superior orbital fissure.
steps.tip: Apical crowding threatens vision; report it explicitly.

steps.label: Bones and sinuses
steps.detail: Review fractures, herniated contents, entrapment configuration and sinus source of infection.
steps.look: Coronal bone windows of the floor and medial wall; adjacent sinuses.
steps.normal: No orbital fracture; adjacent sinuses clear.
findings: Orbital floor blowout fracture __ mm with herniation of fat and the inferior rectus.
Trapdoor fracture with the inferior rectus caught in the defect (child).
Ethmoid sinusitis as the source of orbital cellulitis.
steps.tip: A muscle in the fracture does not by itself prove clinical entrapment; describe the configuration.

steps.label: Sinus distribution
steps.detail: Describe each sinus and the pattern of disease, including unilateral patterns.
steps.look: Coronal images through the frontal, ethmoid, maxillary and sphenoid sinuses.
steps.normal: Paranasal sinuses clear.
findings: Mucosal thickening of the [maxillary] sinuses bilaterally.
Unilateral complete opacification of the [ ] sinus (consider obstructing lesion or fungal disease).
Air–fluid level in the [ ] sinus.
steps.tip: Unilateral disease needs a cause: tumour, dental source, fungal disease or a polyp.

steps.label: Drainage pathways and nasal cavity
steps.detail: Assess the ostiomeatal units, frontal and sphenoethmoidal recesses, septum, turbinates and dental source.
steps.look: Coronal images for the ostiomeatal complex; sagittal for the frontal recess.
steps.normal: Ostiomeatal units, recesses and nasal cavity patent.
findings: Obstruction of the [left] ostiomeatal unit.
Nasal polyps filling the nasal cavity.
Periapical lucency of the [ ] molar with maxillary sinusitis (odontogenic source).

steps.label: Operative anatomy and variants
steps.detail: Report skull-base asymmetry, lamina papyracea, optic nerve and carotid relationships and relevant variants.
steps.look: Coronal images of the cribriform plate and ethmoid roof; sphenoid sinus walls.
steps.normal: No dehiscence or relevant surgical variant.
findings: Asymmetric ethmoid roof, lower on the [ ].
Dehiscent lamina papyracea on the [ ].
Onodi cell with the optic nerve running through it.
Dehiscent carotid canal in the sphenoid sinus.
steps.tip: Surgical variants that put the orbit, optic nerve or carotid at risk should be stated explicitly.

steps.label: Focal tissue and bone
steps.detail: Separate secretions from an enhancing mass and assess remodelling, erosion and diffusion.
steps.look: T2 and post-contrast MRI; bone windows on CT.
steps.normal: No focal mass; no bone erosion.
findings: Enhancing mass with a convoluted cerebriform pattern (inverted papilloma pattern).
Expansile non-enhancing sinus with thinned walls (mucocele).
Destructive enhancing mass with restricted diffusion (malignancy to be excluded).
steps.tip: Secretions change signal with protein content; only enhancing tissue is tumour.

steps.label: Extension beyond the sinus
steps.detail: Review the orbit, pterygopalatine and infratemporal fossae, cavernous sinus, dura and brain.
steps.look: Post-contrast fat-suppressed MRI of the orbit, fossae and anterior cranial fossa.
steps.normal: No orbital, fossa or intracranial extension.
findings: Orbital subperiosteal abscess.
Extension into the pterygopalatine fossa.
Dural enhancement / epidural abscess.
steps.tip: Invasive fungal sinusitis can spread along vessels and nerves with little bone destruction.

steps.label: Oral phase
steps.detail: Assess bolus control, preparation and transfer.
steps.look: Lateral fluoroscopy of the oral cavity with each consistency.
steps.normal: Normal bolus control and transfer; no oral residue.
findings: Premature spillage of liquid into the pharynx before the swallow.
Oral residue after the swallow.

steps.label: Pharyngeal phase
steps.detail: Describe swallow initiation, pharyngeal propulsion and clearance.
steps.look: Lateral and frontal views of the pharynx during the swallow.
steps.normal: Timely swallow initiation with complete pharyngeal clearance.
findings: Delayed swallow initiation with bolus in the pyriform sinuses.
Residue in the valleculae and pyriform sinuses [bilateral / asymmetric].
steps.tip: Asymmetric residue on the frontal view suggests unilateral pharyngeal weakness.

steps.label: Airway protection
steps.detail: Record penetration or aspiration, its timing and the cough response.
steps.look: Lateral view of the larynx during each swallow; note before, during or after the swallow.
steps.normal: No laryngeal penetration or aspiration.
findings: Laryngeal penetration to the vocal folds, cleared.
Silent aspiration of thin liquid [during] the swallow (no cough).
Aspiration after the swallow from pyriform sinus residue.
steps.tip: Silent aspiration — without cough — carries the greatest risk; state the cough response.

steps.label: Structural findings
steps.detail: Assess pharyngeal pouches, webs, osteophytes and upper oesophageal sphincter opening.
steps.look: Lateral view of the pharyngo-oesophageal segment.
steps.normal: No diverticulum, web or cricopharyngeal impression.
findings: Zenker diverticulum __ mm above the cricopharyngeus.
Prominent cricopharyngeal bar narrowing the lumen by __%.
Postcricoid web.
Anterior cervical osteophytes indenting the pharynx.

steps.label: Manoeuvres and limitations
steps.detail: Record the response to tested modifications and incomplete coverage.
steps.look: Document each consistency and manoeuvre tested and whether the cervical oesophagus was assessed.
steps.normal: Consistencies tested: [ ]. No manoeuvres required. Cervical oesophagus clear.
findings: Chin-tuck eliminated aspiration of thin liquid.
Thickened liquid swallowed safely.
Examination limited by [patient cooperation / positioning].

steps.label: External and middle ear
steps.detail: Assess the canal, tympanic membrane, scutum, ossicles and middle ear recesses.
steps.look: Axial and coronal thin sections; follow malleus, incus and stapes; Prussak space and scutum on coronal images.
steps.normal: External canal and middle ear clear; scutum sharp; ossicular chain intact.
findings: Soft tissue in Prussak space with blunting of the scutum and medial displacement of the ossicles (pars flaccida cholesteatoma).
Erosion of the [long process of the incus / stapes superstructure].
External auditory canal exostoses.
steps.tip: Scutum erosion with soft tissue in Prussak space is the classic sign of acquired cholesteatoma.

steps.label: Mastoid and tegmen
steps.detail: Describe aeration, septal erosion, tegmen defects and the mastoid cortex.
steps.look: Coronal images of the tegmen tympani and mastoideum.
steps.normal: Mastoid well aerated; tegmen intact.
findings: Opacified mastoid with erosion of the septa (coalescent mastoiditis).
Tegmen defect __ mm [with soft tissue herniation].
Postoperative mastoid cavity.
steps.tip: Mastoid opacification alone does not prove coalescent mastoiditis; look for septal erosion.

steps.label: Inner ear
steps.detail: Inspect the otic capsule, cochlea, vestibule, semicircular canals, windows and vestibular aqueduct.
steps.look: Axial images at the cochlea and vestibule; Pöschl reformats for the superior canal.
steps.normal: Cochlea, vestibule and semicircular canals normal; otic capsule intact; normal vestibular aqueduct.
findings: Lucency anterior to the oval window (fenestral otosclerosis).
Enlarged vestibular aqueduct (__ mm at its midpoint).
Dehiscence of the superior semicircular canal.
Cochlear malformation: [ ].

steps.label: Facial nerve and vascular channels
steps.detail: Review the facial nerve canal, carotid canal, jugular bulb and sigmoid plate.
steps.look: Follow the facial canal (labyrinthine, tympanic, mastoid segments); check the jugular bulb height and plate.
steps.normal: Facial nerve canal intact; normal carotid canal, jugular bulb and sigmoid plate.
findings: Dehiscent tympanic segment of the facial nerve canal.
High / dehiscent jugular bulb.
Aberrant internal carotid artery crossing the middle ear.
steps.tip: An aberrant carotid or dehiscent jugular bulb is a retrotympanic "mass" that must not be biopsied.

steps.label: Focal lesion, trauma or device
steps.detail: Describe a focal lesion, fracture course, otic-capsule involvement or implant position.
steps.look: Fracture course relative to the otic capsule; implant electrode position in the cochlea.
steps.normal: No focal lesion, fracture or device.
findings: Otic-capsule-sparing fracture with ossicular disruption.
Otic-capsule-violating fracture through the cochlea.
Cochlear implant electrode array fully inserted in the scala tympani.
Enhancing middle ear mass (paraganglioma pattern).

steps.label: Symptom and coverage
steps.detail: Record pulsatile or non-pulsatile tinnitus and side, and whether the protocol covers the right structures.
steps.look: Pulsatile: temporal bone CT and arterial and venous imaging. Non-pulsatile: MRI of the internal auditory canals.
findings: [Right] pulsatile tinnitus: temporal bone CT with CT angiography.
[Left] non-pulsatile tinnitus with hearing loss: MRI of the internal auditory canals.
steps.tip: The work-up depends on whether the tinnitus is pulsatile; say what the protocol can and cannot show.

steps.label: Internal auditory canal and cerebellopontine angle
steps.detail: Inspect the vestibulocochlear nerves and look for a mass.
steps.look: High-resolution T2 and post-contrast T1 of the internal auditory canals.
steps.normal: Internal auditory canals and cerebellopontine angles normal.
findings: Enhancing intracanalicular mass __ × __ × __ mm (vestibular schwannoma pattern).
Vascular loop in the internal auditory canal (common, often incidental).

steps.label: Middle ear and bone
steps.detail: Assess middle ear soft tissue and dehiscence or variants of vascular canals.
steps.look: Temporal bone CT for the jugular bulb, carotid canal and sigmoid plate.
steps.normal: No middle ear mass; normal vascular canals.
findings: Enhancing mass on the cochlear promontory (glomus tympanicum).
Dehiscent sigmoid sinus plate / sigmoid sinus diverticulum.
Dehiscent jugular bulb.

steps.label: Arteries and veins
steps.detail: Review arterial stenosis, dissection, aneurysm and aberrant course, and venous sinus stenosis or diverticulum and signs of shunting.
steps.look: CT or MR angiography and venography; early venous filling as a sign of arteriovenous shunting.
steps.normal: No arterial or venous abnormality; no signs of arteriovenous shunting.
findings: Transverse sinus stenosis (idiopathic intracranial hypertension context).
Carotid dissection / fibromuscular dysplasia.
Early venous filling with enlarged occipital artery branches, suspicious for a dural arteriovenous fistula.
steps.tip: A routine negative MRI does not exclude a dural arteriovenous fistula.

steps.label: Concordance and limits
steps.detail: Match the finding to the side and symptom type and separate a plausible cause from an incidental variant.
steps.look: Side of the finding versus the side of symptoms.
steps.normal: No cause for the tinnitus identified on this protocol.
findings: Ipsilateral [finding] is a plausible cause.
Findings are contralateral / incidental.
Catheter angiography would be needed to exclude a fistula.

steps.label: Thyroid background
steps.detail: Measure both lobes and the isthmus and describe parenchymal echotexture and vascularity.
steps.look: Transverse and longitudinal views of each lobe; Doppler.
steps.normal: Normal-sized thyroid with homogeneous echotexture.
findings: Diffusely heterogeneous, hypoechoic parenchyma with increased vascularity (thyroiditis pattern).
Enlarged multinodular goitre.

steps.label: Nodule location and size
steps.detail: Number each clinically relevant nodule, record side and pole and measure three dimensions.
steps.look: Transverse (width and AP) and longitudinal (length) measurements; compare with prior.
steps.normal: No thyroid nodule.
findings: Nodule 1: [right] [lower] pole, __ × __ × __ mm (previously __ × __ × __ mm).
steps.tip: Give each nodule a stable number and location so follow-up compares the same nodule.

steps.label: TI-RADS features and points
steps.detail: Score composition, echogenicity, shape, margin and echogenic foci and add the points.
steps.look: Composition 0–2, echogenicity 0–3, shape 0 or 3 (taller-than-wide on transverse), margin 0–3, echogenic foci 0–3 (add all foci types).
findings: Solid (2), hypoechoic (2), wider-than-tall (0), smooth (0), no foci (0): 4 points, TR4.
Spongiform (0): TR1.
Solid (2), very hypoechoic (3), taller-than-wide (3), irregular (2), punctate foci (3): 13 points, TR5.
steps.tip: Measure taller-than-wide on the transverse view; comet-tail artefacts score 0.

steps.label: Extrathyroidal extension and nodes
steps.detail: Assess extrathyroidal extension, tracheal relationship and suspicious cervical nodes.
steps.look: Nodule capsule; central and lateral neck nodal levels.
steps.normal: No extrathyroidal extension; no suspicious cervical nodes.
findings: Extrathyroidal extension into the strap muscles.
Suspicious [right level III / IV] node with microcalcifications / cystic change / loss of hilum.
steps.tip: A suspicious node needs sampling even when the nodule itself is small.

steps.label: Recommendation
steps.detail: Combine TR category, size, prior cytology and context into an explicit recommendation.
steps.look: ACR thresholds: TR3 FNA ≥2.5 cm (follow-up ≥1.5 cm); TR4 FNA ≥1.5 cm (follow-up ≥1.0 cm); TR5 FNA ≥1.0 cm (follow-up ≥0.5 cm).
findings: TR[ ], __ mm: fine-needle aspiration recommended.
TR[ ], __ mm: ultrasound follow-up in [ ].
Below the ACR thresholds: no follow-up required.
steps.tip: The ACR algorithm does not apply to nodules that already have benign cytology unless there is growth.

steps.label: Brainstem and root entry zone
steps.detail: Inspect the trigeminal nuclei and root entry zone for infarct, demyelination or mass.
steps.look: Axial T2/FLAIR and DWI of the pons; post-contrast T1.
steps.normal: No brainstem lesion at the trigeminal nuclei or root entry zone.
findings: Demyelinating plaque at the [right] trigeminal root entry zone.
Pontine infarct involving the trigeminal nucleus.

steps.label: Cisternal segment and neurovascular contact
steps.detail: Describe vessel contact, its site and nerve displacement, indentation or atrophy.
steps.look: High-resolution 3D heavily T2-weighted images with MR angiography; compare sides.
steps.normal: No neurovascular contact with the cisternal trigeminal nerves.
findings: Contact of the [superior cerebellar artery] with the [right] nerve at the root entry zone, with nerve indentation and atrophy.
Simple vascular contact without morphological nerve change.
Venous contact.
steps.tip: Neurovascular contact is common in asymptomatic people; nerve displacement or atrophy near the root entry zone is more significant.

steps.label: Meckel cave
steps.detail: Assess nerve and ganglion size, the CSF space and abnormal enhancement or mass.
steps.look: Coronal and axial post-contrast T1 and T2 of Meckel cave.
steps.normal: Meckel caves symmetric and normal.
findings: Enhancing mass in the [left] Meckel cave (schwannoma / meningioma pattern).
Loss of CSF in Meckel cave with enhancement.

steps.label: Cavernous sinus and foramina
steps.detail: Trace V1, V2 and V3 through the cavernous sinus and foramina.
steps.look: Coronal post-contrast images; foramen rotundum (V2) and ovale (V3).
steps.normal: Cavernous sinus and foramina normal.
findings: Enlargement of foramen ovale with an enhancing V3.
Cavernous sinus mass involving V1/V2.

steps.label: Peripheral course and denervation
steps.detail: Review perineural tumour spread, masticator muscle denervation and extracranial causes.
steps.look: Pterygopalatine fossa, masticator space and face within the coverage.
steps.normal: No perineural spread or masticator denervation.
findings: Perineural spread along V[2] from a [facial skin / sinonasal] primary.
Masticator muscle denervation atrophy on the [ ].
Coverage does not include the full peripheral course.
steps.tip: A study limited to the cisternal segment can miss distal perineural disease.
